title: Mission priority file
description: Swappable input that sets what matters on this mission. The jury may hand us an unseen one, so the governor validates it before use and refuses a bad file with the field that is wrong, keeping the previous file meanwhile. YAML may write crew levels unquoted; the loader validates the file's JSON form, where they are strings.

weights.description: Weight 0 to 1 for every capability name a guest card can return.

mission_critical.description: Mission-critical guests (B.0): response class 60 S, the last to give power, one step per tick within the 60 s full sequence.

shed_order.description: Optional declared shed order, keyed by capability name like weights. Precedence: safety-critical guests are never shed and hard limits come first; throttles come before sheds; then the response class (5 S before 60 S, never 200 MS); throttles before sheds inside each class; then this order; then the least mission value lost per kW freed. A positive rank goes before every unlisted capability (1 first), a negative rank after them (-1 last); unlisted capabilities keep the computed order in between, and equal ranks fall back to it. A name that no loaded guest card returns is refused.

confirm.description: Optional crew policy per rule, keyed by rule name (rules in config/assumptions.yaml), replacing that rule's default at the crew levels given. confirm: a human confirms live; standing_plan: approved before it is needed; automatic; forbidden. Nobody aboard can confirm at 0 (brief A.6), so confirm is refused there. A rule name the ship profile does not define is refused.

response.description: Optional response classes (A.8, DEC-60). The brief's ceilings are the degradation priorities, in a fixed order: safety_command (200 MS) is never shed and ArgOS only stops, holds or secures it; mission_critical (60 S) gives power last, one step per tick after a fresh reading, within 60 s of the fault; every other guest is shed_first_action (5 S) and gives power in the first action, within 5 s. A card's safety_critical is always 200 MS; a profile may add guests to it, never remove one.

0.description: No live confirmation with nobody aboard (brief A.6).
